speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand what is going on with your child's skin lesions, could you please tell me the patient's age and how long these lesions have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Can you describe the appearance of the papules in more detail, specifically if they are umbilicated (have a central dimple) and what color they are? Also, has the child had any fever or other systemic symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The description of skin-colored, pearly, umbilicated papules is highly characteristic of Molluscum contagiosum. Given the daycare exposure and typical presentation, I am confident in my assessment.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
